samples.identity: GitHub HTML source view of darkoperator/Posh-SecMod PostExploitation module
evidence: Magic and HTML parsing identify a complete GitHub source-view page, despite the .psm1 filename. There are no inline event handlers, javascript: links, exploit objects, or executable PowerShell script elements.

The 1652 rawLines in application/json reconstruct upstream source SHA-256 21e577ac4e1199aff6c4dd53b78ee15b6361dc9ce4e1b22db4b44f8db255797a, ignoring the trailing newline. The raw source was fetched with forager and retained in scratch with its provenance.

Module load defines functions without invoking the payloads. Generators return caller-addressed reverse-shell, download/execute, SAM hashdump, or NTDS-copy source as text or Base64/Deflate text. Start-PostRemoteProcess accepts an operator command, computer and credentials for Win32_Process.Create.

The hashdump template enables SeDebugPrivilege, duplicates the LSASS token, assigns it to the thread, reads LSA boot-key classes and SAM F/V data, and derives LM/NT hashes with MD5, RC4 and DES. The reverse-shell template couples a caller-selected TCP stream to COMSPEC stdin/stdout. These supported generated-code observations are retained.

The NTDS template requests a VSS snapshot, copies NTDS.dit to TEMP, deletes its snapshot and restores service state; one WMI lookup contains a spelling error, so runtime success is not presumed. IIS helpers explicitly recover application-pool, virtual-directory and database-connection credentials on invocation.
The one literal encoded-command example decodes to write-host hello world; arbitrary payloads and listener addresses are caller inputs, not preconfigured attack infrastructure.

Fetched GitHub entry modules and static imports implement React rendering, code-view navigation, clipboard copying, contrast cookies, module registration, and browser telemetry. The source text is displayed, not submitted to a PowerShell evaluator.
samples.context_missing: No deployment history, operator authorization, or host activity was supplied. Official upstream audit-tool provenance and the absence of autonomous attack configuration tip the judgment.
samples.possible_external_label_reason: The offensive source includes reverse-shell, hashdump, token impersonation and credential-recovery code; a content signature or collection of a source-view URL could produce the malware label.

evidence: An independent Esprima parse confirms exactly one assignment to CKEDITOR.lang[hr]. Its RHS contains only ordinary nested objects with literal values; no calls, getters, computed properties, appended statements, obfuscation, network access or executable payload.

The core editor, editorPanel and common tables equal the official CKEditor 4.3.0 source tables, including every nested common translation. The remaining table entries are editor-plugin UI labels. This comparison identifies the component without asserting an exact release of the bundled build.

The sole URL is the copyright comment licensing link. Forager retrieved the CKEditor Licensing page. Clipboard, upload, email and dictionary-server wording are UI translations, not implementations of those operations.
samples.possible_external_label_reason: Likely a benign resource collected with a hostile web application or an overbroad script heuristic; the feed provided no explanation or deployment context.

samples.identity: CKEditor 4 Canadian French core/plugin translation table

Core translation tables match official CKEditor 4.3.0 source. Remaining entries are editor-plugin UI labels; English SCAYT fallback strings describe UI behavior without implementing it.

Retains bracket and dotted forms, whitespace tolerance, quoted/read near misses, and appended-behavior coverage. Rejects non-table assignments that the old name incorrectly identified as language tables. No YAML consumer or suppressor depends on this identity.

Matcher, platform/type scope, confidence and notable criticality unchanged. Generic FileName syntax cannot identify a browser control. Updated its sole explicit ActiveX consumer, preserving the hostile CLSID-plus-assignment combination.

Bare DeflateStream supports both directions. Matcher and full effective scope/criticality are unchanged. The decompression composite retains the mode reference and now describes co-occurring evidence. All three encoded-carrier consumers updated. The LSB directory consumer gets the explicit relocated atom to preserve its member set; compression-library selectors already include codec. Existing .ps1 and HTML decompression positives retained.
